memory_candidates.content: When a repository consumer decides to delete a file that other tooling auto-creates on absence, grep is not enough to find every auto-create site: a duplicate, informal copy of the same 'if file missing, create default template' logic can live in a Markdown skill/command spec alongside the canonical script implementation (e.g. commands/todo.md and skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md both independently documented the same ROADMAP.md auto-create step that roadmap-integration.sh itself also performed). Fixing only the script leaves the prose copy to silently undo the fix on the next command run. Search skill/command Markdown prose for the same trigger phrase ('Ensure X exists', 'If the file does not exist, create it') as well as the script logic before declaring an absence-handling fix complete.

A resync-mode deploy (deploy-headless.sh without --wipe) does not delete files that were removed from an extension manifest's provides.scripts -- it only stops recopying them. After quarantining a script (removing it from provides.scripts and git-mv-ing it to scripts/deprecated/), a stale copy can linger in the deployed .claude/scripts/ tree and trip a whole-tree orphan-detection gate (find_orphans) on the next verify-deploy.sh run. The fix is a direct rm of the stale deployed file (safe: .claude/ is a disposable, gitignored deploy artifact) rather than a --wipe, which is needlessly destructive for a single stray file.

Editing a markdown file registered in an extension's index-entries.json (line_count field) will trip check-extension-docs.sh's Rule R (line-count mismatch) on the next doc-lint run unless the index entry's line_count is updated in the same change. This applies per-extension (core/index-entries.json, literature/index-entries.json, etc.) -- any content edit to a file with an index entry needs a companion line_count fix, discoverable only by actually redeploying and running the doc-lint gate, not by static review alone.
